# A restored layout brings the tabs back but not the tab you were on: the topology diff has no active-item category

## Context

The operator's requirement for dock layouts is *"reload the multi-window app with the saved layout ⇒ getting the same multi-window setup."* #18252 / PR #18253 made the restore path reachable at all — the seams it needs had no implementer. This is the next measured thing between that path and the sentence: **a restored layout brings the tabs back, but not the tab you were on.**

Promotion of a defect-note (ticket-create §1e), on the operator-escalation trigger: the active tab is part of "the same setup".

## Measured at `dev@274b63beac`

Real capture, real reconciler, a real workspace (the arm added by PR #18253, `test/playwright/unit/dashboard/DockTopologySeams.spec.mjs`):

| hop | `nodes['main-tabs'].activeItemId` |
|---|---|
| capture | `strategy` — **kept**, the record is complete |
| live composition moves on | `swarm` |
| after `TopologyReconciler.reconcile()` | `swarm` — **the live value survives** |

Tab membership and order restore correctly in the same run. Only the active item does not.

## The chain, verified end to end

1. `model/TopologyReconciler.mjs:606` delegates each slot to `RestorePlanner.restoreToward(live, captured)`.
2. `persistence/RestorePlanner.mjs` builds its plan **entirely** from `TopologyDiff.diffDockDocuments(current, captured)`, emitting `addTab`, `moveItem`, `resizeSplit`, `setItemAutoHidden`.
3. `model/TopologyDiff.mjs:105` returns exactly six categories:

```js
{moves: [], adds: [], removes: [], resizes: [], tabReorders: [], autoHideFlips: [], unchanged: [], errors: []}
```

**There is no active-item category.** The planner cannot emit what the diff never reports, so the string `activeItemId` appears nowhere in `TopologyDiff.mjs`, `RestorePlanner.mjs` or `TopologyReconciler.mjs`.

It is unaddressed rather than declined — no comment anywhere argues that the active tab is runtime-only state, and the capture format keeps it, which is the opposite argument.

## The verb already exists

`model/Operations.mjs:253` implements `setActiveItem(document, {tabsNodeId, itemId})`, registered in the operation table at `:46` and classed `topology` at `:87`. Nothing new is needed in the model — this is a diff category and one plan step.

## Proposed change

- `TopologyDiff` gains an active-item category for tabs nodes whose `activeItemId` differs between current and captured, in the same shape as the existing ones (`{nodeId, from, to}`).
- `RestorePlanner` emits `setActiveItem` for each, ordered **after** the adds/moves/reorders — the active item must be a member of the node when it is set, so a step that runs before its own item arrives would be rejected by the executor.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 — A restore returns the captured `activeItemId` for every tabs node. Red-first: the arm in `DockTopologySeams.spec.mjs` currently pins the live value surviving, and that pin flips to the captured value.
- [ ] AC-2 — Ordering: the emitted `setActiveItem` runs after the item it names has arrived in the node. An arm covers the case where the active item is one the restore had to `addTab` or `moveItem` first.
- [ ] AC-3 — A node whose active item is already correct emits **no** step. Restore plans stay minimal; a no-op step is a spurious commit.
- [ ] AC-4 — An active item the capture names but the restore cannot place (it landed in `surplus`, or the node no longer exists) does not emit a step and does not fail the restore. Restore never destroys, and it must not start throwing here either.
- [ ] AC-5 — Mutation-verified: removing the emit reds AC-1's arm, and removing the ordering rule reds AC-2's.

## Non-goals

- The single-window (`captureScope: 'window'`) path, unless it shares the planner — measure, do not assume.
- Focus. Which tab is ACTIVE is document state; which element has DOM focus is not, and restoring focus is a separate question nobody has asked for.
- Any change to the capture format. It already carries the value.

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029`. No new concept: an existing model verb reaches an existing plan.
